newsitem.title: JAPAN: Typhoon Opal has little impact on Japan refineries.
newsitem.headline: Typhoon Opal has little impact on Japan refineries.

text.p: Production at oil refineries in Japan has been largely unaffected by Typhoon Opal, although loading and unloading at some plants located near the path of the storm has been temporary halted, spokesmen for refinery firms said on Friday.
"The typhoon has had no impact on production at our plants," said a spokesman for Tonen Corp, which runs a 166,000 barrel-per-day (bpd) plant in Arita, Wakayama prefecture in western Japan.
He also said that the temporary disruption in loading and unloading did not threaten normal operations, as the plant has plentiful crude oil supplies and sufficient tank space to store oil products.

Typhoon Opal, packing maximum winds of 108 kph (68 mph), was located about 60 kilometres (38 miles) east-southeast of Owase, Mie prefecture in central Japan at 9.00 a.m (0000 GMT), and was soon expected to hit Aichi and Shizuoka prefectures on the Pacific coast, the Meteorological Agency said.

Other oil firms with refineries near the path of the typhoon, including Toho Oil Co Ltd's 35,000-bpd refinery in Owase, said that their plants are running normally and that no disruption is expected in their production despite the temporary halt of loading and unloading operations.
